sentences.text: Austrocheirus was a medium-sized theropod dinosaur measuring between 5.5 and 6.5 meters in length.
The generic name Austrocheirus means "southern hand," while the specific epithet isasii honors the discoverer and preparator Marcelo Pablo Isasi.
This species is notable for being the first known mid-sized abelisauroid that did not have the reduced forelimbs typical of its clade.
While initially estimated at 7 to 8 meters, the length of Austrocheirus was revised to 5.5 meters in 2016.
Fossils of Austrocheirus were discovered on March 17, 2002, in the Pari Aike Formation.
The genus Austrocheirus was named and described by Martin Ezcurra, Federico Agnolin, and Fernando Novas in 2010.
Remains were found in the Cerro Fortaleza Formation in southern Patagonia, Argentina.
Austrocheirus is classified as a reptile within the phylum Chordata, belonging to the order Saurischia and the suborder Ceratosauria.
Cladistic analysis initially placed Austrocheirus in a basal position within Abelisauroidea, more derived than Ceratosaurus and Berberosaurus.
Due to conflicting evidence, some researchers suggest classifying Austrocheirus as incertae sedis within Averostra until more material is found.
In a 2024 study, Hendrickx et al. placed Austrocheirus in a new clade called Berthasauridae, alongside Berthasaura and Afromimus.
The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Austrocheirus as Noasauridae.
Austrocheirus lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
Austrocheirus lived approximately 96.2 million years ago during the Cenomanian stage in what is now South America.
Originally dated to the Maastrichtian (71–66 million years ago), the fossils were later re-dated to the Cenomanian (approximately 96.2 million years ago).
The time range for Austrocheirus is recorded as the Campanian stage, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
Oliver Rauhut challenged the classification of Austrocheirus as an abelisauroid in 2012, arguing that its defining features are also found in non-abelisauroid theropods.
